### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ff3e6de8627121a0035a548971a6a4d3d8b40501` — the merge of head `ed18660403e13dfee68d9f80d277ab49bebd5cf7` into base `e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ff3e6de8627121a0035a548971a6a4d3d8b40501 && git checkout ff3e6de8627121a0035a548971a6a4d3d8b40501
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71 ed18660403e13dfee68d9f80d277ab49bebd5cf7 && git checkout -B drift-repro e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71 && git merge --no-ff ed18660403e13dfee68d9f80d277ab49bebd5cf7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e35db835b41ff5afd4c366500796453016a89c71` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-secret-internal-fields.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/error-http-status-spelling.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/secret-field-own-ref-write.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/secret-field-own-ref-write.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, .changeset/27582-secret-field-own-ref-only.md + packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-credentials.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-channel.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-client-secret.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-headers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-secret.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx, .claude/agents/os-dev.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Read at 2026-10-29T20:40Z: card #27582 (body, triage 6498936750, claim 6500815103, os-dev-report 6506504333 at 2026-10-29T19:36Z), PR #27695 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...pr27695b` (7 files, +597/−6; the head's last commit moves only the changeset, the code is 75e18b19's), and the head's 54 check-runs: 39 `success`, 15 `skipped`, 0 other. Every required context that runs on a PR is green (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` 1–8 and aggregate, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` twice, the later at 2026-10-29T20:27Z); the dogfood shards are `skipped` by ci.yml's own two-speeds rule (`github.event_name != 'pull_request'`), so no PR run measures the dogfood corpus. Security card: this record states rules and code, never a procedure.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rule, as ruled and as coded.** Triage ruled fail-closed: a non-system write may only seal a new value or keep its own record's ref. The ref branch of `encryptSecretFields` now does exactly that: `context?.isSystem === true` keeps the pass-through; otherwise the write's own stored rows are read once (`ownRows ??=`), the ref is kept only when there is at least one own row and every own row holds exactly that value in that column, the key is then dropped (as the echoed mask is), and anything else throws `SecretRefWriteError` before any `sys_secret` row or record statement. Nothing is looked up about what the ref names, so the two refusals (a ref that resolves, a ref that resolves to nothing) are one answer, and the message names the column and never the value (unit test pins message equality and non-containment; dogfood pins it over REST).
- **Completeness over the engine's write doors.** `engine.ts` issues a record statement with a caller payload at exactly three exits, and each is behind a call site of `encryptSecretFields`: the insert loop (single, batch, and `insertMany`, which is `insert` with `__partialRowErrors` — the credential pass sits inside the same per-row `try`, so partial mode reports the refused row and lands the rest), the by-id update (driver exit `driver.update` or `updateByIdExpecting` under an ADR-0142 precondition), and the predicate update (`driver.updateMany`). The remaining `driver.create` sites in the file are the insert's own autonumber-resync exit. There is no engine `upsert` verb; the protocol's `batchData` upsert arms call `createData`/`updateData`. `cloneData` reads the source through `engine.findOne` (so a `secret` column arrives as the read mask), then `engine.insert`s the copy: the mask is dropped before the ref branch, so a clone is not refused and, as before this PR, carries no credential. The import doors (`/import`, `/import/jobs`) run `runImport` under the caller's context through the protocol's create/update faces; the undo door restores `before` snapshots that `captureBefore` takes from the engine-read `existing` row, i.e. the mask or null, never a ref. No writer outside the engine touches a `secret` column: the three credential channels (`connector-credentials.ts`, `flow-credential-channel.ts`, `sso-client-secret.ts`) write plaintext under `SYSTEM_CONTEXT`, and the webhook hooks compose plaintext into `headers_secret`/`signing_secret` inside the engine write. Judgment: no non-system path reaches a `secret` column without the rule.
- **The sole bypass.** `isSystem` is never resolved from the wire: every HTTP context is assembled with `isSystem: false` (`assemble-execution-context.ts`, `entryFields`), no REST route reads a context off the body or query, and every `{ ...ctx, isSystem: true }` spelling in `rest`/`core`/`objectql` is server-side elevation (import-job bookkeeping rows, hook/flow `runAs: 'system'`, seed, migration). Row 23e's sentence "Inbound HTTP never carries the flag" is true of the code. The elevation surfaces a hook or flow author holds inherit the pass-through by design; the row's "Lose" column says so.
- **Verdict-to-statement window.** By-id: the pre-image is `readUpdatePriorRow`'s driver-level read (declared columns only, the caller's tenant/transaction bag), the not-found gate runs between that read and the call site, so `[null]` never reaches the check, and the statement writes the same id. Predicate: the D7 memo (`readPriorRows`) binds the middleware-composed AST and a `buildDriverOptions` bag; the statement binds the same AST and the same bag rebuilt from the same inputs, and inside an open transaction the same unit. The window is harmless by construction: a kept ref removes the key, so the statement never writes the column; a refusal writes nothing; a row that joins or leaves the match set between read and statement changes nothing about that column. Zero matched rows is refused (nothing to keep), which is the fail-closed arm.
- **Legitimate callers.** Console password field: `OBJECTUI_SECRET_MASK` is echoed for a held value and dropped before the ref branch (dogfood pins the GET then PATCH round trip). Export then import: the export reads through the engine, so the file carries the mask, which the import drops. Clone: masked read, see above. Import undo: masked `before`. Seed replay and migration: system. A `beforeUpdate` hook that spreads `previous` into the payload keeps the record's own ref (unit test). The only class newly refused is the ruled one.
- **Tests and ablations.** 19 unit cases over a real engine and a statement-recording stub driver (the pins include "the statement does not carry the column" on by-id and predicate keeps), 5 dogfood cases at the REST data door with a provider wired, the status-spelling registration; red first at bf7eff90; seven clause ablations plus a dist leg each red, restores proven blob == HEAD. The battery is adequate for the rule.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/objectql': patch` with `fix(objectql)!:`, a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start in both the PR body and the changeset, a remedy paragraph, and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition: correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right — nothing an author writes in metadata changes; a record value is not metadata. The disposition fits: no schema key moves, and the package's published surface is unchanged — the new symbols (`SecretRefWriteError`, `StoredRowsReader`, the two constants) live in `engine-secret-internal-fields.ts`, which neither `index.ts` nor `core.ts` re-exports and which `package.json` `exports` (`.` and `./core` only) does not reach; a consumer branches on `code`/`status`, the pair `EmptyCredentialWriteError` already carries. `Check Changeset` is green on this head. `Skills-docs: none` is present as the narrowing rule requires.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dogfood battery owed and not taken (REWORK condition).** `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` Definition of done: the full dogfood suite runs once at the final head whenever the title carries `!` or `Clause-②:` carries the `(narrowing)` arm, no shard, no path; `review-checklist.md`: before enqueue the seat verifies `dogfood_battery` pinned to the head, full, reds fixed or reported, and "missing or narrowed ⇒ REWORK". The os-dev-report declares `dogfood_battery: n/a — no '!' in the PR title and no (narrowing) arm`; the head under review carries both (title `fix(objectql)!:`, changeset and body `no (narrowing)`, added after that report). What ran is 9 credential-channel dogfood files (60/60) at 75e18b19, a narrowed battery, and CI's dogfood shards do not run on a PR. So no full-corpus measurement of this narrowing exists. The code is byte-identical to 75e18b19, so the run is owed, not a change.
2. **Declared deviation, accepted.** The claim allowed `engine.ts` only to pass the system flag; the diff passes each call site's own stored rows instead. The ruling's "its own record's ref" cannot be judged without the row, the flag was already in reach, and nothing else in `engine.ts` moved. Declared in Acceptance notes.
3. **Residual on stored state, rule level only.** Values stored before this change are not re-examined (the PR says so). The existing sweeps (`os secret orphans`, `sys-secret-orphan-report.ts`, `secret-reference-union.ts`) classify unreferenced handles; none classifies a handle held by more than one holder, or held by a column other than the one it was minted for (`releaseSecretHandles` asks that question only at deletion). A report-only sweep of shared references is owed as a follow-up card; the seat files it, with the usual security discipline.
4. **Preview asymmetry, pre-existing.** `ObjectQL.validate()` runs no credential pass, so a write preview cannot predict this refusal, exactly as it could not predict the empty-credential one. Unchanged by this PR; noted, no fix owed here.
5. `open_questions: []` in the report; none added by this review beyond item 3.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-secret-internal-fields.ts` — holds. The branch is placed after the empty-string refusal and before the provider gates, so the verdict depends on the payload and the record, never on what is wired. `StoredRowsReader` keeps the read demand-driven (called only when a non-system payload carries a ref) and memoised across a payload's secret fields. `every` over `own?.[field] === value` is strict and fail-closed; `null` from the reader is `[]`, refused. Dropping the kept key mirrors the mask drop and is what makes the window argument hold. The error carries `code`, `status`, `httpStatus`, `object`, `field`, named `SecretRefWriteError`. No must-fix, no should-fix.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` — holds. Three call sites, each naming its own rows correctly (none, the pre-image, the memo), docblock updated to the new rule, nothing else moved. No must-fix, no should-fix.
- `packages/objectql/src/error-http-status-spelling.test.ts` — holds: the new refusal is registered and both spellings agree at 400.
- `packages/objectql/src/secret-field-own-ref-write.test.ts` — holds: every door, both arms, the system pass-through, identical answers, the column-absent statement pins, hooks on both verbs. No gap that changes the verdict.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/secret-field-own-ref-write.dogfood.test.ts` — holds: the REST doors (`POST`, `createMany`, `import`, `PATCH`), stored value read at driver level, `sys_secret` count unchanged across refusals and keeps, one answer for two refusals.
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` — holds: row 23e states Get/Lose truthfully against the code; the census register line names `encryptSecretFields` with one elevation read; `check:system-context-census` is green inside `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- `.changeset/27582-secret-field-own-ref-only.md` — holds, see ②.
- Must-fix: **M1** — run the full dogfood battery at the final head (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the lock, no shard, no path), fix or report any red, and record it as `dogfood_battery` pinned to the head in the PR body; then a new record on this head. No code change is expected from it.
- Should-fix: **S1** — file the follow-up card for the report-only shared-reference sweep (③ item 3), stated at rule level.
